finalText:
I've written proposals to move the four remaining canvases to maude-v2, but nothing has switched yet. In this project, switching a design system is a review you apply yourself, so I didn't edit any canvas or `.meta.json` file. The fifth canvas, `ui/v2/00 Index`, was already on maude-v2.

The proposals and an overview, `review.md`, are in `.design/_runs/b01df2eb-0596-4c74-ad44-42046e8a4c89/ds-switch/`:

- **ui/panels/GitPanel** (5 artboards)
- **ui/panels/DiffView** (3 artboards)
- **ui/panels/GitHubIdentity** (5 artboards)
- **ui/panels/RepoBranchSwitcher** (6 artboards)

The studio's own preview of the switch marks all four as ready to move: nothing keeps any of them on maude, and nothing was refused.

**What each switch changes:**
- The system setting goes from `maude` to `maude-v2`.
- The two style imports point to the maude-v2 files.
- The outer wrapper `className="maude"` becomes `className="ds"`. Without this the switch doesn't work: maude-v2 only applies its colours and type inside `.maude-v2` or `.ds`, so the artboards would show up unstyled.
- Every token the canvases use also exists in maude-v2.

**What will look different:** the accent changes from indigo to azure. Selected rows and highlights become see-through tints instead of solid colours. Buttons, chips, focus rings and the "Add this draft" button all change colour.

**Decisions for you:**
1. GitPanel, GitHubIdentity and DiffView draw the Maude logo inline, copied from the old system. Compare it with the maude-v2 logo.
2. All four canvases are marked handed-off, so the built app will still be on the old system. Decide whether to hand them off again.
3. Once these move, nothing will use the old `maude` system. Keeping or deleting it is up to you.

**Left as is:** a sample file path in GitPanel's mock change list, comments in the `.css` files that still name `system/maude`, and some hard-coded font sizes and spacing. None of these affect the switch.

To apply, run `maude design ds switch --all --to maude-v2`. It's one step in Version history, so ⌘Z undoes it. Then take a screenshot of the four canvases to check them.
